overview:
China is a vast country in East Asia, the third or fourth largest in the world by area at about 9.6 million km², and home to about 1.4 billion people, second only to India. It stretches from the Himalayas and the deserts of the far west to a long Pacific coastline, and it shares borders with 14 countries, more than any other nation except Russia.

The capital, Beijing, holds the Forbidden City, once home to emperors, while Shanghai is a giant port of skyscrapers. Most people speak Mandarin Chinese, the most spoken first language on Earth, though many regions have their own dialects; all are written with the same characters, a system thousands of years old.

China is governed by the Communist Party, which has held power since 1949, with the government based in Beijing. Since the late 1970s it has grown from a poor farming nation into the world's biggest manufacturer, building high-speed railways, huge cities and space rockets. The island of Taiwan governs itself, though China claims it as part of its territory.
landAndNature:
China's land tilts from the high Tibetan Plateau in the west, the "roof of the world" at more than 4,000 meters, down to fertile plains in the east. Mount Everest, on the border with Nepal, is the highest point on Earth. The Yangtze, Asia's longest river, and the Yellow River, cradle of Chinese civilization, both begin on the plateau and flow east to the sea. The Gobi and Taklamakan deserts fill the north and west, and in the south, limestone hills near Guilin rise like green teeth from the rivers.

Climates range from Siberian cold in the northeast to tropical heat on Hainan Island. Giant pandas munch bamboo in the mountain forests of Sichuan, and China also shelters golden snub-nosed monkeys, Siberian tigers, Chinese alligators and the Yangtze finless porpoise.
peopleAndCulture:
About nine in ten people belong to the Han Chinese group, while 55 recognized minorities, including Tibetans, Uyghurs, Mongols and Zhuang, keep their own languages and traditions. Family is central to life, and the Lunar New Year, or Spring Festival, sends hundreds of millions of people home for dumplings, red envelopes of money and fireworks. Other holidays include the Mid-Autumn Festival with mooncakes and the Dragon Boat Festival with paddling races.

Chinese cooking varies by region, from Sichuan's fiery chilies to Cantonese dim sum, all eaten with chopsticks. Tea has been drunk here for thousands of years. Calligraphy, kung fu, opera and paper-cutting are treasured arts, and table tennis, badminton and basketball are the favorite sports. China's inventions include paper, printing, gunpowder, the compass, silk and porcelain.
history:
Farming villages along the Yellow River grew into China's first dynasties more than 3,500 years ago; the Shang wrote on oracle bones, the earliest Chinese writing. In 221 BC Qin Shi Huang united the warring states as the first emperor, began the Great Wall and was buried with an army of thousands of terracotta soldiers. Dynasties rose and fell for 2,000 years, including the Han, the glittering Tang, the Song, the Mongol Yuan, the Ming and the Qing.

In the 1800s Britain and other powers forced China into unequal trade treaties after the Opium Wars. The last emperor fell in 1911, and after Japanese invasion and civil war, Mao Zedong's Communists founded the People's Republic in 1949. Mao's policies caused a terrible famine and the chaotic Cultural Revolution. From 1978 Deng Xiaoping opened the economy, lifting hundreds of millions out of poverty.
funFacts: China spans five geographical time zones but uses only one, so in the far west the sun can rise at 10 a.m.
All the sections of the Great Wall added together stretch more than 21,000 kilometers.
Toilet paper was first used in China more than 1,400 years ago, reserved at first for emperors.
China's high-speed rail network is the longest in the world, with more than 40,000 kilometers of track.
Fortune cookies were invented in the United States, not China, and are almost unknown there.
The Lunar New Year travel rush is the largest annual movement of people on Earth, with billions of trips.
